title: 4-bit Adder With Carry
statement:
Add two 4-bit values and a carry-in, producing a 4-bit sum and a carry-out.

## Your entity

```
entity solution is
    port (
        a    : in  std_logic_vector(3 downto 0);
        b    : in  std_logic_vector(3 downto 0);
        cin  : in  std_logic;
        sum  : out std_logic_vector(3 downto 0);
        cout : out std_logic
    );
end entity solution;
```

`sum` is `a + b + cin`, truncated to 4 bits; `cout` is `'1'` exactly when
that addition would not have fit in 4 bits -- the bit that a 4-bit register
has nowhere to put.

`"0111" + "0001"`, `cin = '0'` -- 7 + 1 -- gives `sum = "1000"`,
`cout = '0'`: 8 fits in 4 bits.
`"1111" + "0001"`, `cin = '0'` -- 15 + 1 -- gives `sum = "0000"`,
`cout = '1'`: 16 does not.

## Input and output

The testbench reads one line of stdin as three space-separated tokens --
`a`, `b` (4-character bit strings) and `cin` (a single `'0'` or `'1'`) --
drives them onto the matching ports, waits for the outputs to settle, and
writes `sum` immediately followed by `cout` back out on one line (five
characters: four for `sum`, one for `cout`).

## Watch out

- `unsigned(a) + unsigned(b)`, both 4 bits wide, produces a 4-bit result --
  numeric_std's `"+"` does not grow the result to fit an answer that
  overflows, it wraps, the same way a 4-bit register genuinely would. That
  4-bit wrapped value *is* the correct `sum` in every case (truncating and
  wrapping mean the same thing here), but the bit that fell off is now
  nowhere: nothing in a 4-bit `unsigned` can tell you afterwards whether it
  carried out or not. `cout` needs an answer wide enough to still have that
  bit *before* anything gets truncated back down to `sum`.

tests.name: carry out
tests.description: 15 + 1 = 16 -- the sum wraps to 0000 and the carry is the only place 16 shows up. A solution that ties cout to '0' passes the case above and fails this one.

tests.name: carry in tips it over
tests.description: 7 + 8 = 15 fits, but the carry-in makes it 16 -- cin has to be added before the overflow check, not after.

tests.name: everything set
tests.description: 15 + 15 + 1 = 31 -- the largest possible result, exercising every sum bit alongside the carry.
